attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, offered as his definition of AGI and his assessment of it.

semantics.note: The garbled 'has not achieved' plainly means 'has not been achieved'. The normalised claim keeps his definition (anything a human can do, autonomously) and states it as a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Snapshotting at publication and reading AGI as broad autonomous human-level capability is a fair, ordinary reading. Requiring evidence on breadth, autonomy and human-relative performance together is reasonable.

evidence.note: A May 2026 preprint proposing a framework for measuring progress toward AGI. It says no clear framework exists, but it does not assess whether any system met the definition on June 4–5.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only a measurement-framework preprint. Nothing assesses the leading systems around June 4–5, 2026 for broad autonomous human-level capability, and nothing shows such a system existed. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met by the evidence in the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence describing Anthropic's June 4 blog.

semantics.note: The normalised claim faithfully restates his description of what the blog's results bear on.

contract.note: The result depends on reading 'not AGI' as 'the results do not establish AGI' rather than 'the results have no bearing on AGI'. That reading is ordinary in context, since Marcus has just contrasted RSI with AGI. The contract flags the choice.

evidence.note: This is the blog itself, which is the object of the claim, so it counts as direct evidence of its own contents. It reports coding, research-reproduction and task-length benchmarks and frames them as a route to RSI. It does not show broad autonomous human-level capability.

reviews.rationale: The blog's results are about coding benchmarks, research reproduction, task length and the speed of AI development, and the blog presents them as a possible path to RSI. None of them shows Marcus's broad, autonomous AGI. Under the contract's reading of 'not AGI', the description holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. The quoted RSI definition is Anthropic's, but he uses it only to frame his own assessment.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps 'so far', the coding-tool characterisation, 'some' code optimisations, and the point that RSI has not been reached and remains speculative.

contract.note: Reading 'humans can leverage' as humans supplying the essential goals and direction is an ordinary reading. The contract notes that 'coding tool' undersells the autonomy agents have within assigned tasks.

evidence.note: The blog says outright that Anthropic is not yet at RSI and that RSI is not inevitable. It describes AI as speeding up a development process that humans still lead. Because the claim is about what the blog showed, the blog itself is direct evidence.

An April 2026 Anthropic post in which agents propose ideas and run experiments on a research problem that humans assigned. This qualifies the 'coding tool' framing, but it does not show autonomous development of a successor. It also predates the June report.

reviews.rationale: The core claim holds: the blog itself says full RSI has not been reached, and the work it describes is human-directed help with development. Calling it a 'coding tool' understates the agents' autonomy within tasks (e2), but humans still set the goals, so the contract's support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'Will require' is unhedged, so this is a scored forecast about a necessary condition for reaching AGI. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Separating necessity from mere use, and requiring an independently confirmed AGI plus a record of how it was developed, is fair to the wording. With no deadline, only a conclusive event can resolve the claim.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, an independent evaluator, reported in September 2026 that Astra made major gains on ARC-AGI-3 but said explicitly that it is not claiming AGI. This does not meet the early-resolution rule and says nothing about which methods are necessary.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no independently confirmed AGI with a documented development route appears before the evaluation date. The strongest candidate event, Astra, was expressly not called AGI. The forecast is not due to be scored and has been neither confirmed nor refuted.
